Development of Novel Methodology for the Utilization of Phosphogypsum in the Low-lying Areas

Abstract:

In the current investigation, for the development of novel methodologies describing the utilization of legacy Phosphogypsum in reclamation of low-lying area, systematic experiments are proposed. By analysing the literature, the methodology for the above stated has been proposed. The proposed methodology is based on achieving a minimum leaching rate and permeability lower than 10-7 cm/s. The literature reveals that by using limestone/slaked lime, the leaching rate can be significantly decreased. The presence of limestone/ slaked lime in the acidic zone enhances the pH and in turn, the mineral dissolution rate decreases. &nbspDue to the above discussed, the leaching rate significantly declines and also the concentrations of Fluoride, Lead, Cadmium and Arsenic in leachate. The current proposed scheme consists of an alternating layer of Limestone/ Slaked lime and Phosphogypsum at a ratio of 1:6 (v/v) for the elimination of disadvantages observed in case of use of mixture of Limestone/Slaked lime and Phosphogypsum.&nbsp In case of column studies, three different columns (SW-846 methods 1314, US EPA 2019c) comprising pure Phosphogypsum, pure Phosphogypsum and Limestone placed alternatively and pure Phosphogypsum and Slaked lime placed in alternate layers will be used. The leaching studies in column illustrate that with increasing liquid-to-solid ratio, the leaching rate of Fluoride, Lead, Cadmium, Sulphate and Arsenic decline. The maximum Fluoride concentration in leachate is found to be 22 mg/L and the lead concentration is 0.022 mg/L. The analysis on Cadmium and Arsenic ensures the safe limit.

Key words: Phosphogypsum, Leaching, Limestone, Slaked lime, Residence time, Reaction time, Dissolution time.
